description:
# RAOM safe recovery and watchdog protection

1. Kind: improve. Depends on completed ITM-0007. Extend delivered RAOM without reopening its completed record.
2. Add explicit operator-requested transition from safe mode to normal mode during current boot. Accept command only when valid current mode is safe. Reject normal, missing, or invalid mode without changing services or recovery state.
3. Acknowledge repaired reset condition so prior reset evidence cannot immediately trigger safe mode again after recovery or reboot. Preserve reset history. New resets must still trigger safe mode when configured threshold is exceeded. NTP and other decision errors retain configured policy.
4. Persistent acknowledged reset baseline is a proposed mechanism, not approved design. Planner must define exact command, evidence boundary, persistence, counter discontinuities, and behavior when evidence is unavailable. Do not silently disable threshold or error protection.
5. Fix shipped safe MONIT profile to enable native full watchdog protection for MONIT. MONIT remains sole supervisor of client-defined safe services. Watchdog checks must work in safe mode without requiring intentionally disabled normal services. Client retains safe service inventory ownership; Cloudflare provisioning remains excluded.
6. Preserve verified hardware feeding during mode transition, MONIT stop/start, and watchdog handoff. Full watchdog must activate only after selected MONIT instance is verified. Prevent competing watchdog and keepalive feeders.
7. Define coherent failure and retry behavior for recovery. Serialize with existing service actions. Do not report successful recovery until normal profile is running and required watchdog protection is verified. Planner must specify interrupted transition recovery and behavior after profile, storage, or service failures.
8. Reuse RAOM locking, state publication, MONIT validation, native service adapters, shared logging, and root checks. Consume existing scr-resets-monitor evidence interface. Limit any dependency changes to demonstrated recovery needs; no general reset-monitor or watchdog redesign.
9. Deliver updated unified scr-raom Debian package and operator documentation, including Structured English algorithm, recovery procedure, watchdog behavior, and failure limits. Use dpkg-based installation, upgrade, rollback, and package verification rather than manual payload copies.
10. Acceptance covers safe-only command enforcement, successful same-boot recovery, no retrigger from acknowledged evidence across reboot, retained history, new threshold violations, error policy, safe service supervision, MONIT watchdog protection in both modes, and transition failure behavior.
11. Keep mandatory repository gates and applicable locked disposable-image restoration checks distinct from focused acceptance tests. Preserve original images and historical package evidence. Mark hardware-required; require identified target/image, exact package hash, explicit operation authority, logs, rollback, and developer hardware confirmation before DONE.
12. Out of scope: automatic recovery, permanent threshold bypass, history deletion, client service deployment, Cloudflare, unrelated OS repairs, and unapproved hardware operations. Existing service selection stays fixed within boot except authorized explicit recovery introduced here.
13. Intake authorizes mint only. No implementation, plan approval, device operation, or chain execution is authorized. Resolve load-bearing recovery and watchdog questions during independent planning.
